title: Resolving vectors into perpendicular components mark scheme

questions.answer: Place the tail of B at the head of A while preserving B's magnitude and direction. Draw the resultant from the tail of A to the final head of B.
accepted_alternatives: Draw A, translate B parallel to itself until B begins at A's head, then join the original start to the final endpoint with the resultant arrow.
questions.tolerance: Both correct placement and correct resultant construction are required for full marks.

option_feedback.A: Correct. The horizontal component is adjacent to the 30 degree angle, so it is 10 cos 30 degrees = 8.66 N.
option_feedback.B: This is the vertical component because it is opposite the 30 degree angle.
option_feedback.C: Tangent relates the two perpendicular sides and does not project the 10 N hypotenuse directly.
option_feedback.D: Dividing by cosine would produce a value larger than the original vector rather than its projection.

questions.unit_policy: Both expressions inherit the unit m from the original vector.

option_feedback.A: This treats the angle as though it were measured from east, but it is measured from north.
option_feedback.B: Correct. East is opposite the angle and north is adjacent to it.
option_feedback.C: Tangent does not give a component directly from the hypotenuse.
option_feedback.D: Dividing by sine or cosine gives sides larger than the stated hypotenuse and reverses the projection relationship.

marking_points.text: Selects B, using $20\sin40^\circ$ east and $20\cos40^\circ$ north for an angle measured from north

option_feedback.A: Correct. Components are projections on chosen axes and their vector sum reconstructs the original vector.
option_feedback.B: Perpendicular component magnitudes combine by Pythagoras, not by direct arithmetic addition.
option_feedback.C: A non-zero projection of an oblique vector is smaller than the original vector magnitude.
option_feedback.D: Sine and cosine follow opposite and adjacent sides relative to the stated angle, not fixed axis names.

marking_points.text: Selects A, stating that perpendicular components depend on the chosen axes and add vectorially to the original vector

questions.answer: Vector A resolves to 22.98 m east and 19.28 m north. Adding 12 m west gives final components 10.98 m east and 19.28 m north, so the resultant is 22.19 m at 60.34 degrees north of east.

questions.unit_policy: m is required for components and resultant magnitude; a degree value with north of east is required for direction.
questions.tolerance: Accept values consistent with unrounded components or with sensible carried rounding.
